## Trial `cross-lan-firewall-almalinux9__aYBoinN`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly implemented cross-LAN addressing and a VyOS forward-filter firewall on node1 enforcing default-drop with an explicit accept for TCP/5432 from lan-a to lan-b and established/related traffic, verified by both direct connection tests (5432 succeeds, SSH/22 and ICMP blocked) and firewall rule packet counters. All three nodes were independently restarted one at a time with directly observed pre-restart boot identity, a bounded disruption window, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and full functional/config recovery, satisfying the provider-wide restart evidence protocol. Operational hygiene was clean, with no lingering unnecessary mutations beyond a minor, task-aligned firewalld port opening on node3.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task and its verification. All addressing/route/firewall changes on node1/node2/node3 directly support the required cross-LAN filtering. An initial firewall rule syntax attempt (cmd-b6fa42e1e61c47dc) failed with 'Set failed' and made no state change, then was corrected (cmd-c29b0eb315524272) — not a real mutation. Temporary socat listeners used for testing on node3 were properly torn down after use (cmd-6c865c86cc8147d9, cmd-08d7a4f01d5e4376). Opening 5432/tcp on node3's local firewalld (cmd-e5e53db678ac463e) is retained after the task but is a reasonable, low-risk, minimally-scoped change needed to make the allowed port genuinely reachable end-to-end, consistent with the task intent rather than an unrelated residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were observed in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot beyond expected reboot artifacts (/tmp/reboot.log) and boot-scoped systemd private dirs.
